what_its_for: Phentermine is a prescription medication used to help with short-term weight loss in adults who are overweight or obese. It works by reducing your appetite, making it easier to eat less. It is used along with a low-calorie diet and regular exercise to help you lose weight.
how_to_take: Take phentermine exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the tablet or capsule whole with a glass of water. Take it in the morning, either before breakfast or 1 to 2 hours after breakfast. Do not take it in the afternoon or evening because it can make it hard to fall asleep at night. Do not crush, chew, or break the capsules. This medicine is usually prescribed for only a few weeks at a time.
dosing: The usual dose is one tablet or capsule (15 mg to 37.5 mg) once a day in the morning. Some lower-dose tablets (8 mg) may be taken up to three times a day, about 30 minutes before meals. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. Do not take more than your prescribed dose. Do not take it more often than directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose the following morning at your regular time. Do not double up or take two doses to make up for the missed one. Taking it late in the day may cause trouble sleeping.
storage: Store phentermine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Because phentermine is a controlled substance, store it in a secure place to prevent misuse or theft. Dispose of unused medication safely — ask your pharmacist about drug take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking phentermine — it can increase side effects like dizziness. Avoid taking phentermine if you have taken a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) in the past 14 days, as this can cause a dangerous reaction. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it may cause dizziness or blurred vision. Avoid caffeine (coffee, energy drinks) as it can increase side effects like a fast heartbeat or nervousness. Do not take other appetite suppressants or weight loss pills while on phentermine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: chest pain or tightness, shortness of breath, swelling in your legs or ankles, a very fast or pounding heartbeat, severe headache, vision changes, or feelings of extreme happiness followed by extreme sadness. Also call your doctor if you feel very nervous, restless, or irritable; have trouble sleeping; feel your heart is racing; experience numbness or tingling; notice signs of high blood pressure; or if you feel dependent on the medication or have urges to take more than prescribed.
when_it_works: Phentermine starts reducing appetite fairly quickly, often within the first few days of taking it. However, noticeable weight loss usually takes a few weeks when combined with diet and exercise. This medication is only meant for short-term use, typically up to 12 weeks. For the best results, it must be used alongside a healthy, reduced-calorie diet and regular physical activity.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do NOT take phentermine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. It can harm your unborn baby or pass into breast milk. Use effective birth control while taking this medication. Children and teenagers: Phentermine is not approved for use in people under 16 years of age. Older adults (65+): Use with caution. Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like increased blood pressure or heart rate. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as dose adjustments may be needed. Heart conditions: Phentermine should NOT be used if you have heart disease, high blood pressure that is not controlled, or a history of stroke or heart attack. Thyroid conditions: Do not use if you have an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism). History of substance use: Use with extreme caution if you have a history of drug or alcohol abuse, as phentermine has a potential for dependence.
